description: Temporal characterization of the post-2017 displaced rotation structure (step_118's private dipole): free-scan extremeness on the raw field, era x cap factorial, transit-epoch gradient with quality/energy controls, geometry-matched pairs, named-direction audit including the CMB scalar rest frame, and harmonic decomposition.

cmb_cone_coherence.note: post-hoc coherence datum: both comet-channel axes lie on a ~51 deg cone about the CMB dipole axis (opposite lobes)

carrier_matrix.LPC 1902-1950 (three-leg): declared-axis replication p = 0.0056, top 4.6% of 370 trial axes (step_106)

T9_carrier_audit.pattern: 3/3 three-leg records carry the signature; 0/3 single-solution records do -- including the same comets re-fitted under a single joint solution

verdict: The post-2017 displaced structure is a real, resolved feature of the record, not a residual-fitting artefact: on the raw rotation field it is the global maximum of a 612-axis free scan (+0.270 dex at (120,-40), look-elsewhere p=0.0910), and it persists in the better-observed strata.  Inside the displaced cap its amplitude grades with transit epoch -- rho(drot, transit_year) = -0.55 (p=0.00038), surviving controls for observation count, arc and boundary energy, and appearing in the unexplained proper-time channel (rho=-0.38) -- the signature of a temporally graded field feature rather than a solution-quality artefact.  The structure is nevertheless record-specific at cohort level: pre-2018 objects in the same cap show no elevation (median 0.152 vs 0.206, MW p=0.000957) and no temporal gradient.  Geometry-matched pairs (k=3, n=38): post 0.206 vs matched pre 0.152, perm p=0.0009.  The displaced axis sits 54 deg from the CMB dipole apex -- nearer than the declared axis (132 deg) -- and 127 deg from the ISM inflow.  The independent-fitter check closes the solution-lineage channel: SBDB and MPC CometEls elements for the same objects agree to 0.025 deg median in the periapsis direction, so the structure cannot be manufactured by JPL's orbit fits -- it lives in the astrometric record itself.  The signature-morphology discriminator then classifies the structure with its composition control: the raw energy channel reads elevated in-cap (daa 110 vs -266 in/out, p=0.00179), but the contrast decomposes by boundness -- on the bound substratum it is flat (daa 77 vs -100, p=0.15) while the rotation channel there is strongly elevated (drot 0.206 vs 0.099 deg), so the energy-exchange reading is carried by the thin unbound substratum (n=8 in-cap, p=0.000112), whose sign structure -- in-cap unbound members lose energy where out-cap members gain it -- is a directional energy-transfer asymmetry rather than a uniform exchange.  The independent leg decomposition (step_127 backfill / step_128) then shows the slip morphology itself is mirrored between eras: the modern elevation sits on the outbound leg where the historical anomaly sat on the inbound -- the polarity-flip signature of a bipolar field read at opposite sign, not a different signature class.  The carrier audit then reframes the declared-axis absence itself: the unexplained-slip observable -- the disagreement of independent inbound- and outbound-leg solutions after the gravitational leg prediction is removed -- exists only in three-leg records (CODE, Warsaw, LPC; signature present in all three, LPC p=0.0056, top 4.6% of its free-axis scan).  A single joint solution expresses no fit-vs-fit disagreement for the slip to appear in: the same comets re-fitted under SBDB single solutions are flat (n_in=40, MW p=0.41, leg share 0.52).  The post-2017 record therefore could not express the slip even at full strength -- its flatness is a structural absence of the observable's carrier, not a measurement of zero slip.  The degeneracy that remains is lineage: all three-leg catalogues are Warsaw-school products, so a shared-pipeline fit-disagreement artefact predicts the same 3/3-vs-0/3 pattern; resolving it requires three-leg fits on post-2017 astrometry or a non-Warsaw three-leg catalogue.  The CMB-frame dipole ladder (T10) then measures each record's residual m=1 dipole about the scalar-field rest frame: the two records resolving a significant dipole -- CODE (b=-0.235 dex, p=0.00065) and post-2017 (b=+0.226 dex, p=0.0001) -- both place the bipolar dipole axis within 26 deg of the CMB dipole axis but with opposite polarity, while the weaker records are unresolved (Warsaw p=0.21, pre-2018 p=0.08).  The frame-anchored axis is the cross-record invariant; the measured polarity is record-dependent -- the structure the declared-cap test reads as a reversal is the same bipolar field at the opposite sign.
caveats: The transit epoch proxy (discovery year + t_back) is approximate; t_back measures leg-integration time to the 250 AU sphere, not the true crossing date.
tyr is strongly confounded with boundary energy (rho ~ -0.94): the temporal gradient survives energy control at reduced amplitude and should not be over-interpreted as a pure time effect.

Cohort-privacy at matching transit epochs remains the strongest evidence for a record-level origin: if the field pointed at the displaced direction in those epochs, pre-2018 objects crossing then should carry it.  The discriminating residual is whether post-2017 cap members occupy transit geometries the pre-2018 members lack.
